title: Ston Travel Guide: Walls, Oysters & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan your trip to Ston, Croatia. Read practical advice on parking, driving routes from Central Europe, beaches, and the best areas to stay on Pelješac.
intro:
Ston is a historic town at the base of the Pelješac peninsula, known for its 5.5-kilometer 14th-century defensive walls, operational salt pans, and proximity to Mali Ston bay's oyster farms. It suits travelers looking for a base to explore Southern Dalmatia and the islands without the intense crowds and high prices of nearby Dubrovnik. The town centers on history and gastronomy rather than nightlife or resort complexes.

The best time to visit is between May and September. High summer brings hot weather for swimming at nearby Prapratno beach, while the shoulder seasons of May, June, and September offer cooler conditions for walking the walls and touring the region's wineries. Most visitors drive, as public transport options are limited to local bus routes.

areas.name: Ston (Center)
areas.parking: Paid public lots just outside the walls
areas.summary: The main settlement features stone houses, cafes, and direct access to the salt pans and wall entrance. It offers the most dining options and amenities but lacks immediate beach access.

areas.name: Mali Ston
areas.parking: Limited street parking and small paid lots
areas.beach: No traditional beaches; rocky coastal access
areas.summary: A small village on the northern side of the isthmus, connected to Ston by the walls. It is famous for its oyster farms and traditional waterfront seafood restaurants.

areas.name: Prapratno
areas.parking: Large parking area near the ferry and beach
areas.beach: Immediate access to a sandy bay
areas.summary: Located in a bay south of Ston, this area consists mostly of a large campsite, a few apartments, and the ferry port to Mljet. The natural sandy beach is shallow and well-suited for young children.

areas.name: Broce
areas.parking: Free parking typically provided by guesthouses
areas.beach: Concrete slabs and small pebble coves
areas.summary: A quiet, traditional fishing village a short drive south of Ston. It is surrounded by pine forests and offers a slow-paced environment with minimal commercial facilities.

whenToGo: The tourist season runs from May through October. July and August are the hottest and busiest months, with sea temperatures reaching 26°C and accommodation prices at their peak, though Ston remains less crowded than major coastal cities. June and September offer ideal conditions with warm water, lower prices, and temperatures in the mid-20s, making it significantly more comfortable to climb the unshaded defensive walls. Many local restaurants, salt pan tours, and oyster tasting boat trips operate fully during these months. From November to April, the town is very quiet; many tourist-oriented businesses close for the winter, and the weather is too cool for swimming, though the walls and a few local eateries remain open year-round.

faq.question: Is Ston worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, Ston is worth visiting for its 5.5-kilometer medieval wall, historic salt pans, and renowned oyster industry. It serves as an excellent base for exploring the Pelješac peninsula without the high accommodation costs of Dubrovnik.

faq.question: How many days do I need in Ston?
faq.answer: One to two days is sufficient to see the main attractions in Ston and Mali Ston. However, many visitors stay four to seven days to use the town as a practical base for day trips to Mljet, Korčula, and local wineries.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Ston?
faq.answer: Prapratno beach, located three kilometers from the Ston center, is the most popular beach in the area. It features natural sand and shallow water, making it extremely popular during the summer months.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Ston?
faq.answer: A car is highly recommended for a stay in Ston. While you can walk between Ston and Mali Ston, a vehicle is necessary for reaching the best beaches, visiting nearby wineries, or exploring the rest of the Pelješac peninsula.

faq.question: Where to park in Ston?
faq.answer: There are several paid municipal parking lots located just outside the pedestrian-only historic center. Parking fees apply during the tourist season, and spots can fill up quickly in the middle of the day during July and August.

faq.question: Is Ston good for families?
faq.answer: Yes, Ston is good for families seeking a quiet holiday, especially those with young children who will enjoy the sandy, shallow waters of nearby Prapratno beach. However, it lacks the large resort entertainment and water parks found in more commercialized coastal destinations.
